1. (Currently amended) A system for providing security in a computer system, the system comprising:
a ring oscillator configured to generate a plurality of independent first entropy values;
a countermeasure circuit configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values from the ring oscillator and to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a permutation, hash, or bit-mixer function to generate a second entropy value, wherein the countermeasure circuit is specifically configured to mitigate phase tracking attacks on the ring oscillator;
a pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value; and
a cryptographic circuit configured to generate a random number using the pseudorandom number generator and to produce a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number.

2. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the cryptographic circuit being configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes being configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number.

3. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the cryptographic circuit being configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes being configured to at least:
implement a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and
produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key.

4. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the ring oscillator is configured to generate the plurality of independent first entropy values with reduced susceptibility to phase tracking attacks through the countermeasure circuit.

5. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the countermeasure circuit receives the plurality of independent first entropy values from a single ring oscillator hardware source.

6. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the countermeasure circuit receives the plurality of independent first entropy values from a plurality of independent ring oscillator hardware sources.

7. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the function applied by the countermeasure circuit is a permutation function, and the countermeasure circuit being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values includes being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function.

8. (Currently amended) The system of claim 7, wherein the countermeasure circuit being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function includes being configured to:
divide the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values;
apply the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and
concatenate the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value.

9. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the function applied by the countermeasure circuit is a hash function, and the countermeasure circuit being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values includes being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the hash function.

10. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the function applied by the countermeasure circuit is a bit-mixer, and the countermeasure circuit being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values includes being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the bit-mixer.

11. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the countermeasure circuit being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to selectively apply multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function to generate the second entropy value.

12. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the countermeasure circuit being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to the function to generate the second entropy value.

13. (Currently amended) A method of providing security in a computer system, comprising:
receiving a plurality of independent first entropy values from a ring oscillator;
applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a permutation, hash, or bit-mixer function in a countermeasure circuit to generate a second entropy value, wherein the countermeasure circuit is specifically configured to mitigate phase tracking attacks on the ring oscillator;
seeding a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value;
generating a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value; and
producing a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number.

14. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number.

15. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes at least:
implementing a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and
producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key.

16. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the ring oscillator is configured to generate the plurality of independent first entropy values, and wherein receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from the ring oscillator with reduced susceptibility to phase tracking attacks.

17. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from a single ring oscillator hardware source.

18. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from a plurality of independent ring oscillator hardware sources.

19. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a permutation function, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function.

20. (Currently amended) The method of claim 19, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function includes:
dividing the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values;
applying the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and
concatenating the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value.

21. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a hash function, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the hash function.

22. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a bit-mixer, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the bit-mixer.

23. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes selectively applying multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function to generate the second entropy value.

24. (Original) The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to the function to generate the second entropy value.
